def-td-si-quantities.physical_scope: SI types and units used by the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; this item does not define a thermometer calibration or an equation of state.

def-td-si-quantities:
## Definition

This framework uses the modern International System of Units (SI). A scalar quantity has a real numerical value with the stated unit; a vector quantity has a value in the stated real coordinate space with the stated component unit. The numerical coordinates used elsewhere on this page are divided by their displayed SI units before they are placed in a Euclidean coordinate space.

The model's energy coordinate $U$ and its process-transfer values $Q$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are scalar energies measured in joules (J). Volume $V$ is a scalar measured in cubic metres (m³); amount of substance $n_j$ for species $j$ is a scalar measured in moles (mol); and a particle count $N_j$, when separately used in a microscopic model, is dimensionless. Time $t$ is measured in seconds (s), mass $M$ in kilograms (kg), and a translational velocity $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$ with components measured in metres per second (m/s). The physical meanings of $U,Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}$ are fixed by the state and process definitions, not by their units alone.

The relevant exact SI relations are

$$1\,\mathrm J=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm N=1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}},\qquad 1\,\mathrm{Pa}=1\,\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}.$$

The kelvin (K) is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature. The Boltzmann constant has the exact defining value $k_{\mathrm B}=1.380649\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. The mole is the SI unit of amount of substance; the Avogadro constant has the exact defining value $N_{\mathrm A}=6.02214076\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$. When a model uses particle counts, $n_j=N_j/N_{\mathrm A}$. The molar gas constant is derived as $R=N_{\mathrm A}k_{\mathrm B}=8.31446261815324\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. This framework does not set $k_{\mathrm B}=1$. These SI definitions do not themselves introduce a thermodynamic temperature state function or entropy function.

Within the macroscopic framework, $(U,V,n_j)$ are adopted state coordinates. A quantity's status as primitive in this model is separate from whether its SI unit is a base or derived unit.

def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges.physical_scope: Boundary and exchange classifications for the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; no energy-balance law is asserted here.

def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges:
## Definition

A thermodynamic system $s$ is a model-selected body or collection of bodies together with a specified outer boundary $\partial s$. The boundary separates the system from its environment for the purpose of classifying transfers; it need not be a material wall. A compound system has named subsystems inside one outer boundary. Transfers between its subsystems are internal to the compound; only transfers across $\partial s$ are external.

The model specifies which transfers across $\partial s$ are permitted. A system is closed when no matter crosses its outer boundary; energy may cross. A system is open when only the named matter species and other named transfer channels may cross its boundary. A system or compound is isolated when no matter or energy crosses its outer boundary. These terms classify the declared model boundary, not the accuracy with which a real apparatus approximates it.

This boundary classification alone asserts neither an energy-balance law nor equilibration.

def-td-galilean-rest-frame.physical_scope: The Newtonian frame convention and internal-energy split used in this thermodynamic framework, restricted to mechanical models that supply positive mass, center-of-mass data, and Galilean-compatible transformations; no relativistic energy law or dynamical theorem is asserted.

def-td-galilean-rest-frame:
## Definition

For this nonrelativistic framework, a Newtonian event-coordinate domain is the Cartesian product $I\times\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-cartesian-product]]), where $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is an open time interval as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, and $\mathbb R^3$ has the Euclidean inner product and norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (the norm properties follow from [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]); lengths are measured in metres as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. A Galilean inertial chart labels events in such a domain by coordinates $(t,\mathbf x)$. If a second chart uses the translated time domain $I'=I+\tau$, the allowed coordinate changes are
$$t'=t+\tau,\qquad \mathbf x'=R\mathbf x+\mathbf a-\mathbf b t,$$
where $\tau$ is a constant time shift measured in seconds, $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ is a constant spatial translation measured in metres, $\mathbf b\in\mathbb R^3$ is a constant boost velocity measured in metres per second, and $R\in M_{3\times3}(\mathbb R)$ is a dimensionless constant matrix ([[def-matrix-space]]) satisfying $R^{\mathsf T}R=I_3$ using matrix transpose and product ([[def-transpose-of-a-matrix]], [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]), with $I_3$ the identity matrix. In the coordinate formula, $(R\mathbf x)_i:=\sum_{k<3}R_{ik}x_k$ for $i<3$. Thus time is absolute in this model and no Lorentzian structure is used. Here “frame” means this coordinate chart, not an observer congruence or a basis/tetrad field.

For a finite point-mass representation with $N\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]), $N\ge1$, masses $m_i>0$ in kg at positions $\mathbf x_i\in\mathbb R^3$ in metres for $i<N$, assume $M:=\sum_{i<N}m_i>0$ ([[def-finite-sum]]) and define the center-of-mass coordinates by $X_{\mathrm{cm},j}:=M^{-1}\sum_{i<N}m_i x_{i,j}$ for $j<3$; these three real coordinates form $\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}$. The masses are invariant under the allowed chart changes. Other mechanical models must supply their total mass and center-of-mass map; this thermodynamic item does not construct those quantities for a continuum or field model. Every admitted mechanical model must also supply center-of-mass maps and velocities that transform under the displayed Galilean chart changes by $\mathbf X'_{\mathrm{cm}}(t')=R\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t)+\mathbf a-\mathbf b t$ and $\mathbf v'_{\mathrm{cm}}=R\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}-\mathbf b$, where $t'=t+\tau$; these are kinematic compatibility conditions, not dynamical theorems about arbitrary mechanical models. When the model supplies a center-of-mass position $\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}:I\to\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-function-space]]), its velocity at a time $t$ is the componentwise limit $\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}(t)=\lim_{h\to0}(\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t+h)-\mathbf X_{\mathrm{cm}}(t))/h$ through $H_t:=\{h\in\mathbb R:t+h\in I,\ h\ne0\}$ ([[def-function-limit]]), when that limit exists. A center-of-mass rest frame is a Galilean inertial chart in which this velocity is zero; the adopted covariance condition allows the pure boost $\mathbf b=\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}$ to select one whenever the velocity is defined. For a fixed closed body with total mass $M>0$ in kg, its separately tracked translational kinetic energy in a selected inertial chart is $K_{\mathrm{cm}}=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}\|_2^2$ in joules; under a pure boost it is $K'_{\mathrm{cm}}=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}-\mathbf b\|_2^2$.

In this framework $U$ denotes the scalar internal-energy coordinate evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame. Bulk translational kinetic energy and any separately tracked external-field potential energy are excluded from $U$. The model treats $U$ as invariant between rest charts that differ only by spatial translation or orthogonal orientation, and fixes its numerical zero, including any retained or subtracted constituent rest-energy offsets, consistently across the composition changes it admits. This is a nonrelativistic modeling convention, not a derived energy-transformation law.

def-td-equilibrium-state-domain.physical_scope: Equilibrium macrostates of nonrelativistic, macroscopic, simple-compressible systems represented by internal energy, volume, and named mole amounts, with admitted preparations recorded in a supplied center-of-mass rest chart; no stability or constitutive law follows from this definition.

def-td-equilibrium-state-domain:
## Definition

Fix a system $s$ as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]]. A material constitution $c$ specifies a finite ordered list of named species $(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)$, with $r\in\mathbb N$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and $r\ge1$, and the model parameters that identify the material. An equilibrium-preparation label in the set $E_c$ selects a single macrostate that the model designates as an equilibrium state for constitution $c$. The equilibrium designation is primitive model input here; it is not a dynamical equilibration theorem or a global-stability claim. For each admitted preparation, its mechanical model supplies a positive total mass and a defined center-of-mass velocity as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], so the allowed boost can select a center-of-mass rest chart in which its internal energy is recorded. A preparation for which these mechanical data are unavailable lies outside this framework. A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function-space]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.

def-td-process-and-protocol.physical_scope: Process records with equilibrium endpoints and fixed-chart energy bookkeeping in the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; trajectories may include nonequilibrium configurations and carry no regularity assumption unless a subclass adds one.

def-td-process-and-protocol:
## Definition

For a system $s$ of constitution $c$, the process model fixes one Galilean inertial chart $g_s$ for kinetic-energy bookkeeping and transfer records and holds that chart fixed throughout each process. A process record is a tuple
$$P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P).$$
For each finite closed time interval $I_P=[t_0,t_1]\subseteq\mathbb R$ with $t_0<t_1$ as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, its component fields have these types: $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$ are equilibrium endpoint coordinates from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; $Z_s$ is the model-declared configuration space of the system, its auxiliaries and devices; $Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq Z_s$ is the model-declared set of equilibrium configurations and $\xi_s:Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_c$ assigns their state coordinates; $z_P:I_P\to Z_s$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]); $\mathcal K_s$ is the model-declared set of control/contact records and $\kappa_P\in\mathcal K_s$; and $\mathcal R_s$ is the model-declared set of signed transfer records and $r_P\in\mathcal R_s$. These fields form a finite Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]]). The admitted records $\mathcal P_s$ are the model-specified subset of tuples with these types that additionally satisfy $z_P(t_0),z_P(t_1)\in Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}$, $\xi_s(z_P(t_0))=x_P^-$, and $\xi_s(z_P(t_1))=x_P^+$. No continuity or differentiability is imposed on $z_P$, and its values at interior times need not represent equilibrium states.

For an endpoint bookkeeping quantity $F$, write $\Delta F=F_P^+-F_P^-$. A closed record in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] has no matter crossing the chosen outer boundary. The core closed-record class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\subseteq\mathcal P_s$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]) contains only records for which the system has a supplied total mass $M>0$ and defined center-of-mass velocities at both endpoints in the fixed chart $g_s$, so the kinetic energies $K_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm\|_2^2$ are defined as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. It further requires $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$, where $U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ denotes any model-specified external-field potential energy tracked separately from the internal-energy coordinate in $g_s$. Other process classes require an expanded energy bookkeeping rule.

For each $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$, the protocol supplies maps $Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}:\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\to\mathbb R$ whose values are interpreted in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]] and whose energy bookkeeping uses $g_s$. $Q[P]>0$ means energy enters the system through the declared thermal-transfer channel; $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]>0$ means mechanical work is done on the system. These are functionals of the process record, not state functions of $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$. Heat is the protocol-assigned thermal mode of energy transfer, not a quantity stored in the equilibrium state. A record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$. A closed record may still exchange energy; it is not thereby isolated.

A preparation is a model-specified rule selecting the particular initial equilibrium state $x_P^-$. A statistical extension may instead specify a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space, as in [[def-probability-measure]]; such a statistical preparation is outside this deterministic process class. A preparation does not assert later equilibration. An admitted record may pass through nonequilibrium configurations even though both endpoints lie in $D_c$.

post-td-bulk-additivity.physical_scope: Separated macroscopic subsystems in the declared bulk family when interface and long-range interaction energy are excluded; no claim is made for interacting, surface-dominated, or gravitational systems.

post-td-bulk-additivity:
## Postulate

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

post-td-first-law-energy.physical_scope: Closed nonrelativistic macroscopic process records with equilibrium endpoints, fixed material constitution, and zero change in center-of-mass kinetic energy and separately tracked external-field potential energy, all booked in the fixed Galilean chart selected by the process model.

post-td-first-law-energy:
## Postulate

For every admitted $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ with equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$, fixed material constitution, zero change in center-of-mass kinetic energy, and zero change in separately tracked external-field potential energy in the fixed chart selected by the process model, the adopted model balance is
$$U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)=Q[P]+W_{\mathrm{on}}[P],$$
where $U_c$ is the dimensioned energy-coordinate map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]].

Here the internal-energy coordinate is evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], while $Q[P]$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$ are the protocol transfers defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The sign convention is positive $Q$ into the system and positive $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ for work done on it. If $P$ is adiabatic, its defining condition is $Q[P]=0$, so the same adopted balance gives $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)$.

This equation is an adopted physical postulate of the stated framework. It is not deduced here from a mechanical model or from experimental observations. Records with matter exchange or nonzero changes in omitted kinetic or external-field energy require a separately specified balance and are outside this item.

A statistical preparation that instead supplies a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space is as in [[def-probability-measure]] and belongs to a separate statistical branch; it is an element of $E_c$ only if that model also assigns it a single equilibrium macrostate.

Each $e\in E_c$ is assigned a unique coordinate tuple $(U,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, where $U$ is the adopted internal-energy coordinate in joules as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], $V>0$ is volume in cubic metres, and each $n_j>0$ is an amount in moles; the SI unit assignments are those of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. These are real-valued mole amounts in the bulk continuous chart, not integer particle counts. Define the dimensionless numerical coordinates $\hat U=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$, $\hat V=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$, and $\hat n_j=n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. The representation map $\pi_c:E_c\to\mathbb R^{r+2}$ is a function as in [[def-function-space]], sends $e$ to $(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)$, and the equilibrium state domain is its image $D_c:=\pi_c(E_c)\subseteq\mathbb R^{r+2}$ using inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in D_c$, write $U_c(x):=\hat U\,\mathrm J$, $V_c(x):=\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3}$, and $n_{c,j}(x):=\hat n_j\,\mathrm{mol}$ for its dimensioned coordinates. Preparation labels with the same coordinate tuple represent the same thermodynamic state in this framework. Statistical preparations that specify a probability law belong to a separate branch and are not used in this state-domain definition.

For fixed $n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)$ in a chart used by the model, write $\Gamma_{c,n}=\{(\hat U,\hat V):(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)\in D_c\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2$, with inclusion notation as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. This designated slice is a specified nonempty open convex subset. With the dimensionless Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$ of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] (a norm by [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]), openness means that every $z\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ has some $\epsilon>0$ for which $\{w\in\mathbb R^2:\|w-z\|_2<\epsilon\}\subseteq\Gamma_{c,n}$. Convexity means that $(1-t)z_0+tz_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ whenever $z_0,z_1\in\Gamma_{c,n}$ and $t\in[0,1]$, as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Both properties are assumptions about the particular slice, not conclusions about every $D_c$; no coordinate tuple is presumed physically realizable merely because it lies in an ambient Euclidean space. A zero amount for an absent species belongs only to a separately specified boundary domain and is not in this positive-mole chart.

In a simple-compressible chart, volume $V$ is the only mechanical coordinate in the equilibrium representation; composition changes, fields, polarization, surface terms, and other mechanical coordinates require a separately declared state domain and exchange rules. No pressure or reversible-work formula follows from this definition.

def-td-process-and-protocol.physical_scope: Process records with equilibrium endpoints and fixed-chart energy bookkeeping in the nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic framework; trajectories may include nonequilibrium configurations and carry no regularity assumption unless a subclass adds one.

def-td-process-and-protocol:
## Definition

For a system $s$ of constitution $c$, the process model fixes one Galilean inertial chart $g_s$ for kinetic-energy bookkeeping and transfer records and holds that chart fixed throughout each process. A process record is a tuple
$$P=(I_P,x_P^-,x_P^+,z_P,\kappa_P,r_P).$$
For each finite closed time interval $I_P=[t_0,t_1]\subseteq\mathbb R$ with $t_0<t_1$ as in [[def-interval]], measured in seconds, its component fields have these types: $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$ are equilibrium endpoint coordinates from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]; $Z_s$ is the model-declared configuration space of the system, its auxiliaries and devices; $Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq Z_s$ is the model-declared set of equilibrium configurations and $\xi_s:Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}\to D_c$ assigns their state coordinates; $z_P:I_P\to Z_s$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]); $\mathcal K_s$ is the model-declared set of control/contact records and $\kappa_P\in\mathcal K_s$; and $\mathcal R_s$ is the model-declared set of signed transfer records and $r_P\in\mathcal R_s$. These fields form a finite Cartesian product ([[def-cartesian-product]]). The admitted records $\mathcal P_s$ are the model-specified subset of tuples with these types that additionally satisfy $z_P(t_0),z_P(t_1)\in Z_s^{\mathrm{eq}}$, $\xi_s(z_P(t_0))=x_P^-$, and $\xi_s(z_P(t_1))=x_P^+$. No continuity or differentiability is imposed on $z_P$, and its values at interior times need not represent equilibrium states.

For an endpoint bookkeeping quantity $F$, write $\Delta F=F_P^+-F_P^-$. A closed record in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] has no matter crossing the chosen outer boundary. The core closed-record class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\subseteq\mathcal P_s$ ([[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]) contains only records for which the system has a supplied total mass $M>0$ and defined center-of-mass velocities at both endpoints in the fixed chart $g_s$, so the kinetic energies $K_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm=\tfrac12M\|\mathbf v_{\mathrm{cm}}^\pm\|_2^2$ are defined as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]]. It further requires $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$, where $U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ denotes any model-specified external-field potential energy tracked separately from the internal-energy coordinate in $g_s$. Other process classes require an expanded energy bookkeeping rule.

For each $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$, the protocol supplies maps $Q,W_{\mathrm{on}}:\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)\to\mathbb R$ whose values are interpreted in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]] and whose energy bookkeeping uses $g_s$. $Q[P]>0$ means energy enters the system through the declared thermal-transfer channel; $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]>0$ means mechanical work is done on the system. These are functionals of the process record, not state functions of $x_P^-$ and $x_P^+$. Heat is the protocol-assigned thermal mode of energy transfer, not a quantity stored in the equilibrium state. A record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$. A closed record may still exchange energy; it is not thereby isolated.

A preparation is a model-specified rule selecting the particular initial equilibrium state $x_P^-$. A statistical extension may instead specify a normalized probability measure on a declared measurable space, as in [[def-probability-measure]]; such a statistical preparation is outside this deterministic process class. A preparation does not assert later equilibration. An admitted record may pass through nonequilibrium configurations even though both endpoints lie in $D_c$.

post-td-bulk-additivity.physical_scope: Separated macroscopic subsystems in the declared bulk family when interface and long-range interaction energy are excluded; no claim is made for interacting, surface-dominated, or gravitational systems.

post-td-bulk-additivity:
## Postulate

Let $A$ and $B$ be two named subsystems with disjoint physical regions as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], combined as a compound system $A\sqcup B$ inside a declared outer boundary. The model's admitted separated pairs form a specified subset $\mathcal C_{AB}\subseteq D_A\times D_B$ using [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]] and [[def-cartesian-product]]. For every pair $(x_A,x_B)\in\mathcal C_{AB}$, the composition map $\kappa_{AB}:\mathcal C_{AB}\to D_{A\sqcup B}$ is a function ([[def-function-space]]) adopted so the dimensioned coordinates of its output satisfy
$$U_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=U_A(x_A)+U_B(x_B),\qquad V_{A\sqcup B}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=V_A(x_A)+V_B(x_B),\qquad n_{A\sqcup B,j}(\kappa_{AB}(x_A,x_B))=n_{A,j}(x_A)+n_{B,j}(x_B).$$
Here each coordinate function is the dimensioned map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]] for its material constitution, with SI units as in [[def-td-si-quantities]].

Here “extensive coordinates” means precisely the named coordinates declared additive by this postulate. Amount coordinates are aligned by species label; when a species is absent from one subsystem, its zero amount is in a separately declared composition boundary, not the positive-mole chart of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. This is an idealized composition rule: cross-interface and long-range interaction energy is omitted from $U_{A\sqcup B}$, rather than asserted to vanish in nature. The postulate does not assert that every pair of subsystem states is physically admissible.

The framework's bulk family is a tagged family of material types. For each dimensionless scale $\lambda>0$ the model may designate a tag $c^{(\lambda)}$ and a subset $B_{c,\lambda}\subseteq D_c$ of states admitting a scaled copy, with inclusion as in [[def-subset-and-proper-subset]]. For $x=(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n_1,\ldots,\hat n_r)\in B_{c,\lambda}$, the scaling map is the function $\delta_\lambda:B_{c,\lambda}\to D_{c^{(\lambda)}}$ ([[def-function-space]]) given by $\delta_\lambda(x)=(\lambda\hat U,\lambda\hat V,\lambda\hat n_1,\ldots,\lambda\hat n_r)$. The tag matters: $c^{(\lambda)}$ is not silently identified with $c$. This postulate specifies the coordinate scaling model and energy additivity only; it does not postulate entropy additivity or exact scaling for every finite physical body.

This is an adopted physical composition rule, not a deduction from SI units or from the mathematics of Cartesian products.

post-td-first-law-energy.physical_scope: Closed nonrelativistic macroscopic process records with equilibrium endpoints, fixed material constitution, and zero change in center-of-mass kinetic energy and separately tracked external-field potential energy, all booked in the fixed Galilean chart selected by the process model.

post-td-first-law-energy:
## Postulate

For every admitted $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ with equilibrium endpoints $x_P^-,x_P^+\in D_c$, fixed material constitution, zero change in center-of-mass kinetic energy, and zero change in separately tracked external-field potential energy in the fixed chart selected by the process model, the adopted model balance is
$$U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)=Q[P]+W_{\mathrm{on}}[P],$$
where $U_c$ is the dimensioned energy-coordinate map of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]].

Here the internal-energy coordinate is evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame as in [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], while $Q[P]$ and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$ are the protocol transfers defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], in joules as in [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The sign convention is positive $Q$ into the system and positive $W_{\mathrm{on}}$ for work done on it. If $P$ is adiabatic, its defining condition is $Q[P]=0$, so the same adopted balance gives $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=U_c(x_P^+)-U_c(x_P^-)$.

This equation is an adopted physical postulate of the stated framework. It is not deduced here from a mechanical model or from experimental observations. Records with matter exchange or nonzero changes in omitted kinetic or external-field energy require a separately specified balance and are outside this item.

def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline:
## Definition

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.
lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $m,c>0$. Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open set of future timelike vectors and let $f$ be a smooth vector field along the bundle projection $\mathcal V\to M$, with $f(p,V)\in T_pM$ and $g_p(V,f(p,V))=0$. For every initial datum $(p_0,U_0)\in\mathcal V$ satisfying $g_{p_0}(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$, there is a unique local curve $(x,U)$ through it satisfying $D_sx=U$ and $D_sU=f(x,U)/m$. The solution depends smoothly on its initial data and on any finite-dimensional parameters on which $f$ depends smoothly, on a common sufficiently short compact interval near the base datum. It remains on the future unit timelike shell. There is a unique maximal solution on an open interval, but this interval need not be all of $\mathbb R$.
thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization:
## Statement

Let $x:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve on a nonempty open interval $I$, with parameter $s$ and tangent $T=dx/ds$. Fix $c>0$, $s_0\in I$, and $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$, and define $\ell(s)=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}$ and $\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^s\ell(r)\,dr$. Then $\tau'(s)=\ell(s)/c>0$, so $\tau$ is an increasing $C^2$ coordinate on its open image $J=\tau(I)$. The tangent with respect to this parameter is $U=dx/d\tau=cT/\ell$ and satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$. This is a mathematical reparametrization result; by itself it does not identify $\tau$ with a physical clock reading.

post-rpm-test-clock-and-background.physical_scope: Adopted classical test-particle framework on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold; the curved-background clock reading convention extends the flat ideal-clock postulate and is not an empirical accuracy claim.

post-rpm-test-clock-and-background:
## Postulate

**Adopted convention.** On a prescribed background $(M,g,N)$ from [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]], an ideal clock carried along a future timelike test worldline $x$ records the proper-time parameter $\tau$ defined by $d\tau=c^{-1}\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds$. Thus elapsed reading between two ordered points is the integral of this positive density. The flat-spacetime specialization is inherited from [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; extending that convention to the curved prescribed background is a separate adoption of this framework.

When the parameter $s$ is measured in seconds, $x^0=ct$ is in metres, $c$ is in metres per second, and $\tau$ is in seconds. This is a model postulate, not a theorem or a reported measurement. It does not assert that a physical clock realizes the idealization exactly, that the background solves gravitational field equations, or that the test body affects the background.
lem-rpm-length-action-first-variation:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $a<b$, and $x:[a,b]\to M$ a $C^2$ future timelike curve. Put $T=dx/ds$, $\ell=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}>0$, and for a constant $m>0$ and $c>0$ define the length action $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\ell(s)\,ds$. Let $H(\epsilon,s)$ be a $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variation through future timelike curves for $\epsilon$ near $0$, with $H(0,s)=x(s)$ and variation field $J=\partial_\epsilon H|_0$. Then

$$\delta S=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}S[H(\epsilon,\cdot)]\right|_{0}=-mc\int_a^b g\!\left(J,D_s\!\left(\frac{T}{\ell}\right)\right)ds.$$

Consequently $x$ is stationary under all such variations exactly when $D_s(T/\ell)=0$, equivalently $D_\tau U=0$ for the proper-time parameter of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. For any orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\phi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ with $\phi'>0$ and $s=\phi(r)$, the integral and stationarity equation are unchanged. This is a local variational statement; it makes no claim about global proper-time maximality, and the square-root action is not defined for a nonzero null tangent.

post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Classical spinless structureless point test body of constant primitive mass m>0 on a prescribed smooth background; no self-field, radiation reaction, finite-size, quantum, or global-completeness claim.

post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

For a spinless, structureless massive test body of constant primitive mass $m>0$ on a prescribed background satisfying [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]], adopt the action

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds=-mc^2\int d\tau,$$

for future timelike curves, with fixed-endpoint stationary paths as the model's free trajectories. When $s$ is measured in seconds, $T$ has units metres per second; in SI units the action has units joule-seconds. The equality is the proper-time change of variable of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. This is an adopted model premise, not a consequence of the metric or clock postulate. It excludes self-gravity, radiation reaction, spin, finite-size structure, particle creation, and quantum effects; it does not assert empirical adequacy for any particular body.
lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalenc:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $x:[a,b]\to M$ be a $C^2$ curve with parameter $s$ and $T=dx/ds$, fix $c>0$, let $e(s)>0$ be smooth, and let $m\ge0$ be constant. Take independent $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of $x$ and smooth interior variations of $e$. For the action

$$S_e[x,e]=\frac12\int_a^b\!\left(e^{-1}g(T,T)-em^2c^2\right)ds,$$

independent fixed-endpoint variations in $x$ and interior variations in $e$ give

$$g(T,T)+e^2m^2c^2=0,\qquad D_s(T/e)=0.$$

On the future timelike massive branch $m>0$, this constraint uniquely gives $e=\ell/(mc)$, $T/e=mU$, and the action reduces to $-mc\int\ell ds$; in proper-time gauge $s=\tau$, $e=1/m$. On the nonzero future null branch $m=0$, $P:=T/e$ is nonzero future null and $D_sP=0$; if $d\lambda=e\,ds$, then $dx/d\lambda=P$ and $D_\lambda P=0$. There is no null proper-time gauge, and the scale of $P$ remains initial data. Under an orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $s=\phi(r)$ between the parameter intervals, with $T_r=\phi'T$ and $e_r=\phi'e$, the einbein action is invariant.

post-rpm-null-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Separate classical massless test-particle sector with nonzero future-null momentum; no proper-time parameter, no P=mU identification, and no claim of empirical realization.

post-rpm-null-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

Adopt a distinct massless test-particle sector on the prescribed background of [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]]. Its primitive action uses a positive einbein $e(s)$,

$$S_0[x,e]=\frac12\int e^{-1}g(T,T)\,ds,\qquad T=dx/ds,$$

and independent stationary variations in $x$ and $e$. The variational equations and their null branch follow from [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]: the constraint is $g(T,T)=0$, and the physical branch requires $T$ to be nonzero and future-directed. The associated momentum $P=T/e$ is nonzero future null; its positive scale is primitive initial data, not $mU$ for any $m=0$ substitution. Null curves have no proper-time parameter. With $s$ in seconds, $T$ in metres per second, and $e$ in kg$^{-1}$, the integral has units joule-seconds. Under an increasing $C^1$ reparametrization $s=s(r)$, the paired transformation is $T_r=s' T$ and $e_r=s' e$, which leaves the functional invariant by [[lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalence]]; this is the formulation's gauge freedom. Neither the scale nor a clock reading is inferred from the ray image alone.

This is an adopted classical model formulation, not an empirical observation or a theorem. Its scope excludes mass generation, interactions, and quantum field effects.

def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer.physical_scope: Definitions of point-particle momentum and observer-relative energy in the adopted massive and null test sectors; no conservation or empirical claim.

def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer:
## Definition

Use the massive and null sectors as separately adopted in [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]]. For a massive body of constant mass $m>0$, its **mechanical four-momentum** is $P=mU$, where $U$ is its future unit tangent with $g(U,U)=-c^2$. In the null sector, the mechanical four-momentum is the separately specified nonzero future-null vector $P$ from the einbein formulation; no null proper time or $P=mU$ is defined.

At an event, for any observer $n$ of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]], define the spatial momentum and observer energy by

$$q_n(P):=P+g(P,n)n\in n^\perp,\qquad E_n(P):=-c\,g(P,n).$$

The projection identity and positive-definiteness of $n^\perp$ are supplied by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. With SI units, $P$ has units kg m s$^{-1}$, $q_n$ has the same units, and $E_n$ has units joules. This definition is pointwise and does not assert conservation, positivity, or an energy interpretation for an arbitrary vector field that is not an observer.

pthm-rpm-free-massive-and-null-geodesics.physical_scope: Conditional model deduction for free spinless test bodies on a prescribed smooth background; local initial-value solutions only, with no geodesic completeness or empirical universality claim.

pthm-rpm-free-massive-and-null-geodesics:
## Statement

On a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian background, stationary paths of the adopted massive action of [[post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action]] satisfy $D_\tau U=0$ in proper-time parameter, with $P=mU$ and $m>0$ constant. In the separately adopted null sector of [[post-rpm-null-test-particle-action]], stationary einbein paths have a nonzero future-null momentum $P$ satisfying $D_\lambda P=0$ in an affine parameter $\lambda$ with $dx/d\lambda=P$. Through each allowed initial point and tangent, each equation has a unique local solution and a unique maximal solution on an open interval. Neither maximal interval is asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

post-rpm-prescribed-force-law.physical_scope: A selected smooth external force law for a named massive test body of constant mass on a prescribed background; orthogonality is a compatibility condition preserving the mass shell, not a universal force principle.

post-rpm-prescribed-force-law:
## Postulate

For a named massive test body with constant primitive mass $m>0$ and momentum $P=mU$ as defined in [[def-rpm-mechanical-momentum-and-observer-energy]], one may adopt a specified smooth force field $f(x,V)$ on an open neighborhood of the future unit timelike shell within the future timelike velocity cone and the equation

$$D_\tau P=f(x,U),\qquad g(U,f)=0.$$

The orthogonality condition is part of this model's compatibility assumptions: it preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ for constant $m$. It is not a law selecting a force for every particle or interaction. A local IVP follows only where the named force field is smooth, as in [[lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp]]. The force has SI units newtons when $\tau$ is in seconds and $P$ has units kg m s$^{-1}$. No empirical force measurements, universal coupling, or global existence are asserted.

pthm-rpm-killing-particle-charge.physical_scope: Conditional scalar balance for a test particle and a specified Killing field; energy interpretation only for a future unit time-translation field, with no global symmetry assumption.

pthm-rpm-killing-particle-charge:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a smooth Killing field on a region of the prescribed background. For a massive test body obeying the force postulate, with constant $m>0$, $P=mU$ and $D_\tau P=f$, the scalar $g(K,P)$ obeys

$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(K,P)=g(K,f).$$

Thus it is constant when the body is free ($f=0$). For a free null geodesic with affine tangent momentum $P$, $g(K,P)$ is constant along its affine parameter as well. If $K$ is a future unit timelike observer field along the curve, then $-c\,g(K,P)$ has energy units and is the energy defined by that observer; for a general Killing field it is only a conserved scalar, not automatically an energy.

def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline:
## Definition

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.
lem-rpm-shell-tangent-force-ivp:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold and let $m,c>0$. Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open set of future timelike vectors and let $f$ be a smooth vector field along the bundle projection $\mathcal V\to M$, with $f(p,V)\in T_pM$ and $g_p(V,f(p,V))=0$. For every initial datum $(p_0,U_0)\in\mathcal V$ satisfying $g_{p_0}(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$, there is a unique local curve $(x,U)$ through it satisfying $D_sx=U$ and $D_sU=f(x,U)/m$. The solution depends smoothly on its initial data and on any finite-dimensional parameters on which $f$ depends smoothly, on a common sufficiently short compact interval near the base datum. It remains on the future unit timelike shell. There is a unique maximal solution on an open interval, but this interval need not be all of $\mathbb R$.
thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization:
## Statement

Let $x:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve on a nonempty open interval $I$, with parameter $s$ and tangent $T=dx/ds$. Fix $c>0$, $s_0\in I$, and $\tau_0\in\mathbb R$, and define $\ell(s)=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}$ and $\tau(s)=\tau_0+c^{-1}\int_{s_0}^s\ell(r)\,dr$. Then $\tau'(s)=\ell(s)/c>0$, so $\tau$ is an increasing $C^2$ coordinate on its open image $J=\tau(I)$. The tangent with respect to this parameter is $U=dx/d\tau=cT/\ell$ and satisfies $g(U,U)=-c^2$. This is a mathematical reparametrization result; by itself it does not identify $\tau$ with a physical clock reading.

post-rpm-test-clock-and-background:
## Postulate

**Adopted convention.** On a prescribed background $(M,g,N)$ from [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]], an ideal clock carried along a future timelike test worldline $x$ records the proper-time parameter $\tau$ defined by $d\tau=c^{-1}\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds$. Thus elapsed reading between two ordered points is the integral of this positive density. The flat-spacetime specialization is inherited from [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; extending that convention to the curved prescribed background is a separate adoption of this framework.

When the parameter $s$ is measured in seconds, $x^0=ct$ is in metres, $c$ is in metres per second, and $\tau$ is in seconds. This is a model postulate, not a theorem or a reported measurement. It does not assert that a physical clock realizes the idealization exactly, that the background solves gravitational field equations, or that the test body affects the background.
lem-rpm-length-action-first-variation:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $a<b$, and $x:[a,b]\to M$ a $C^2$ future timelike curve. Put $T=dx/ds$, $\ell=\sqrt{-g(T,T)}>0$, and for a constant $m>0$ and $c>0$ define the length action $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\ell(s)\,ds$. Let $H(\epsilon,s)$ be a $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variation through future timelike curves for $\epsilon$ near $0$, with $H(0,s)=x(s)$ and variation field $J=\partial_\epsilon H|_0$. Then

$$\delta S=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}S[H(\epsilon,\cdot)]\right|_{0}=-mc\int_a^b g\!\left(J,D_s\!\left(\frac{T}{\ell}\right)\right)ds.$$

Consequently $x$ is stationary under all such variations exactly when $D_s(T/\ell)=0$, equivalently $D_\tau U=0$ for the proper-time parameter of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. For any orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\phi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ with $\phi'>0$ and $s=\phi(r)$, the integral and stationarity equation are unchanged. This is a local variational statement; it makes no claim about global proper-time maximality, and the square-root action is not defined for a nonzero null tangent.

post-rpm-massive-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Classical spinless structureless point test body of constant primitive mass m>0 on a prescribed smooth background; no self-field, radiation reaction, finite-size, quantum, or global-completeness claim.

For a spinless, structureless massive test body of constant primitive mass $m>0$ on a prescribed background satisfying [[post-rpm-test-clock-and-background]], adopt the action

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int\sqrt{-g(dx/ds,dx/ds)}\,ds=-mc^2\int d\tau,$$

for future timelike curves, with fixed-endpoint stationary paths as the model's free trajectories. When $s$ is measured in seconds, $T$ has units metres per second; in SI units the action has units joule-seconds. The equality is the proper-time change of variable of [[thm-rpm-proper-time-parametrization]]. This is an adopted model premise, not a consequence of the metric or clock postulate. It excludes self-gravity, radiation reaction, spin, finite-size structure, particle creation, and quantum effects; it does not assert empirical adequacy for any particular body.
lem-rpm-einbein-variation-and-equivalenc:
## Statement

Let $a<b$, let $x:[a,b]\to M$ be a $C^2$ curve with parameter $s$ and $T=dx/ds$, fix $c>0$, let $e(s)>0$ be smooth, and let $m\ge0$ be constant. Take independent $C^2$ fixed-endpoint variations of $x$ and smooth interior variations of $e$. For the action

$$S_e[x,e]=\frac12\int_a^b\!\left(e^{-1}g(T,T)-em^2c^2\right)ds,$$

independent fixed-endpoint variations in $x$ and interior variations in $e$ give

$$g(T,T)+e^2m^2c^2=0,\qquad D_s(T/e)=0.$$

On the future timelike massive branch $m>0$, this constraint uniquely gives $e=\ell/(mc)$, $T/e=mU$, and the action reduces to $-mc\int\ell ds$; in proper-time gauge $s=\tau$, $e=1/m$. On the nonzero future null branch $m=0$, $P:=T/e$ is nonzero future null and $D_sP=0$; if $d\lambda=e\,ds$, then $dx/d\lambda=P$ and $D_\lambda P=0$. There is no null proper-time gauge, and the scale of $P$ remains initial data. Under an orientation-preserving $C^1$ diffeomorphism $s=\phi(r)$ between the parameter intervals, with $T_r=\phi'T$ and $e_r=\phi'e$, the einbein action is invariant.

def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space:
## Definition

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, with the geometric meaning fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the future-cone field called $N$ in that definition. A **temporal product chart** is a smooth coordinate map from an open product $I\times\Omega\subset\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ onto an open subset of $M$, with coordinates $(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$. We require $x^0$ to have length units and each $x^i$ to have length units in the physical interpretation.

The chart has **lapse-shift data** $(N,\beta,h)$ when $N:I\times\Omega\to(0,\infty)$, $\beta^i:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $h_{ij}:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are smooth, $h_{ij}=h_{ji}$, and the matrix $(h_{ij})$ is positive definite at each point, with

$$g=-N^2(dx^0)^2+h_{ij}(dx^i+\beta^i dx^0)(dx^j+\beta^j dx^0).$$

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix. The normal field is

$$n=N^{-1}(\partial_0-\beta^i\partial_i).$$

Direct contraction gives $g(n,n)=-1$; require that $n$ is future-directed in the supplied time orientation. This field of observers is distinct from the coordinate vector $\partial_0$, which may be spacelike. The coefficients $N,\beta^i,h_{ij}$ are dimensionless when all four coordinates are in metres. This definition is local to the specified product chart; it asserts no global temporal foliation.
def-rpm-h-almost-regular-legendre:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $\mathcal D$ be an open subset of the time-dependent tangent bundle $\mathbb R\times TQ$ of a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $Q$, and let $L:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R$ be smooth. For fixed $t$, the **fibre derivative** is the map

$$\mathbb F L(t,q,v)=(t,q,p),\qquad p(w)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}L(t,q,v+sw),$$

as in [[def-fibre-derivative-and-legendre-transform-of-a-lagrangian]]. In induced coordinates $p_i=\partial L/\partial v^i$.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantitie.physical_scope: Classical spinless test-particle quantities on a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold. def-rpm-h-background-and-model-quantitie:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Fix a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,T)$ with signature $(-+++)$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Here $T$ denotes the supplied smooth timelike field selecting the future cone, called $N$ in that geometric definition. Use the distinction among a spacetime, a worldline, a pointwise observer, an observer congruence, a tetrad and a chart given in [[def-rpm-spacetime-observer-and-worldline]]. This definition does not make $g$ dynamical.

In this relativistic-particle model, $m>0$ is a fixed **primitive mass parameter** measured in kilograms, and $c>0$ is a fixed **primitive conversion parameter** measured in metres per second. They are parameters of the adopted physical formulation, not quantities derived by this definition. Coordinates $x^a$ in an SI chart have length units; a cotangent vector $p=p_a\,dx^a$ has units of momentum, $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, when all four coordinates are in metres. The canonical one-form $p_a\,dx^a$ therefore has action units $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Along a future-directed timelike curve with tangent $V=dx/d\lambda$, set $s:=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$; then $d\tau=s\,d\lambda/c$, independently of the increasing regular parameter. The length action $-mc\int s\,d\lambda$ has action units. For a future unit observer $n$ and future causal covector $p$, define the model normal-observer energy and spatial momentum covector by

$$E_n(p):=-c\,p(n),\qquad q_n(p):=p+p(n)n^\flat,$$

where $n^\flat=g(n,\cdot)$. The restriction of $g^{-1}$ to covectors annihilating $n$ is positive definite, so it supplies the norm of $q_n(p)$. These are quantity definitions and unit conventions; they do not identify canonical momentum with mechanical momentum, assert that an apparatus measured these values, or establish a dynamical law.
def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system:
## Definition

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.
thm-rpm-h-canonical-poisson-and-flow:
## Statement

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action.physical_scope: Classical spinless structureless point test body with fixed primitive mass m>0 on a prescribed background; excludes self-field, radiation reaction, finite size, spin and quantum effects.

post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action:
## Postulate

For a $C^2$ future-directed timelike worldline $x:I\to M$ on a prescribed smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian background $(M,g,T)$ of signature $(-+++)$, with $m>0$ a fixed primitive mass in kg and $c>0$ in m/s, adopt the stationary-action model

$$S_m[x]=-mc\int_I\sqrt{-g(x',x') }\,d\lambda.$$

Here λ is an increasing regular parameter, endpoint events are fixed, and admissible variations remain future timelike. The integrand is the proper-time length density, so $S_m=-mc^2\int d\tau$; its dimension is action (J s). The adopted premise concerns this ideal free test body only. It is neither a theorem about all matter nor an empirical report, and supplies no backreaction or completeness claim. The flat ideal-clock specialization agrees with [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; adopting this action on a curved background remains a separate premise.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.

post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action:
## Postulate

On a prescribed background $(M,g,T)$, adopt a distinct massless classical particle model with fields $x:I\to M$, $p(\lambda)\in T^*_{x(\lambda)}M$, and a positive smooth multiplier $e(\lambda)>0$:

$$S_0[x,p,e]=\int_I\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Variations of $p,e$ are independent; the physical branch is $p\ne0$, $p^\sharp$ future null. With all spacetime coordinates measured in metres and dimensionless λ, $p_a$ has units kg m/s, $C_0$ has units kg²m²/s² and $e$ has units s/kg, making the action J s. Other parameter units scale $e$ accordingly. This is a separate adopted model: null curves have no proper-time parameter, the model does not arise by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, and its positive momentum scale is additional initial data. On the nonzero branch, the vertical differential is $d_pC_0=p^\sharp\ne0$: nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p\ne0$ give $p^\sharp\ne0$. Hence the shell is a regular primary constraint in the sense of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]]. This postulate is not an empirical observation or a deduction from the massive model.

The cotangent phase-space carrier convention assumes countable choice ACω only; full choice is not assumed.
thm-rpm-h-constraint-consistency:
## Statement

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $(P,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold. Let $\chi_a:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be smooth and suppose the covectors $d_z\chi_a(\lambda,z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in N_\lambda:=\{z:\chi_1(\lambda,z)=\cdots=\chi_r(\lambda,z)=0\}$; this is the regular constraint condition of [[def-rpm-h-regular-constraint-system]] on each slice. Let $H_c:I\times P\to\mathbb R$ be a smooth ambient extension of a specified descended Hamiltonian. Work in a Darboux chart with coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$ and local potential $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$, so $d\theta=-\omega$ under the convention $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$; paths stay in this chart.
For any compact interval $[a,b]\subset I$ with $a<b$, paths $z:[a,b]\to P$ that stay in the chart and smooth multipliers $u^a:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ have action

$$I[z,u]=\int_a^b\left[\theta(\dot z)-H_c(\lambda,z)-u^a(\lambda)\chi_a(\lambda,z)\right]d\lambda.$$

Fixed-endpoint variations of $z$ and unrestricted variations of $u$ imply $z(\lambda)\in N_\lambda$ and $\dot z=X_{H_c(\lambda,\cdot)}+u^a(\lambda)X_{\chi_a(\lambda,\cdot)}$. A trajectory remains in the moving level set only when

$$\partial_\lambda\chi_a+\{\chi_a,H_c(\lambda,\cdot)\}+u^b(\lambda)\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0\quad\text{on }N_\lambda.$$

For constraints independent of $\lambda$, the first term is zero.
thm-rpm-h-first-class-local-reduction:
## Statement

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.
thm-rpm-h-homogeneous-legendre-degenerac:
## Statement

Let $L(q,v)$ be $C^2$ on a conic open subset of a tangent bundle, and suppose $L(q,av)=aL(q,v)$ for every $a>0$ in its domain. At each nonzero $v$,

$$v^iL_{v^i}=L,\qquad L_{v^iv^j}v^i=0,\qquad E_L:=v^iL_{v^i}-L=0.$$

Consequently the velocity Hessian is singular and the fibre derivative cannot be a local diffeomorphism there; a regular Legendre equivalence theorem cannot be applied. These conclusions do not imply that the motion is static or that the Lagrangian has a specified constraint surface.
thm-rpm-h-local-legendre-and-energy-desc:
## Statement

Let $L(t,q,v)$ be smooth on an open velocity domain and let $\mathbb FL(t,q,v)=(t,q,L_v)$ be almost regular in the sense that it is a surjective submersion onto a specified embedded image $N$ and every fibre is connected. Define $E_L=v^iL_{v^i}-L$. Then there is a unique smooth function $h:N\to\mathbb R$ with $E_L=h\circ\mathbb FL$. The assertion is local in the stated domains; no global inverse velocity map is asserted.
thm-rpm-h-second-class-dirac-bracket:
## Statement

Let $(P,\omega)$ be symplectic and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_{2k}$ be smooth on an open set $U$, with $C_{ab}=\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}$ invertible at every point of $U$. Write $C^{ab}$ for its inverse and $N=\{\chi=0\}\cap U$. Then $N$ is an embedded symplectic submanifold, and the bracket

$$\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_a\}C^{ab}\{\chi_b,G\}$$

is the Poisson bracket of the restricted symplectic form on $N$. It is independent of ambient extensions of $F,G$, and every $\chi_a$ is a Casimir. This is local and assumes invertibility on $U$; it does not cover singular points.
thm-rpm-h-flat-shell-global-reduction:
## Statement

In affine Minkowski space with inertial coordinates $x^0,x^i$ measured in metres and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, let $m\ge0$ and let

$$\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p): -p_0=P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2},\ p_0<0\},$$

where $\mathbf p\ne0$ when $m=0$, and write $P^i=p_i$ for the spatial raised momentum components. The characteristic flow of the restricted canonical form is $(x,p)\mapsto(x+\alpha P,p)$, and its orbit space is globally diffeomorphic to $B_m=\mathbb R^3_a\times\mathbb R^3_p$ for $m>0$, or $\mathbb R^3_a\times(\mathbb R^3_p\setminus\{0\})$ for $m=0$, by

$$a^i=x^i-\frac{P^i}{P^0}x^0,\qquad p_i=p_i.$$

The reduced symplectic form is $da^i\wedge dp_i$. The quotient is Hausdorff and second countable and each full characteristic line meets each slice $x^0=ct$ exactly once. This is an explicit free flat quotient, not a conclusion about arbitrary first-class systems.
thm-rpm-h-homogeneous-massive-shell:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $m,c>0$, and $L(x,V)=-mc\sqrt{-g(V,V)}$ on the future timelike tangent cone. Its fibre derivative is

$$p_a=mc\frac{g_{ab}V^b}{s},\qquad s=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}>0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.
thm-rpm-h-regular-local-gauge-slice:
## Statement

Let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ be regular first-class constraints on $N$ as in [[thm-rpm-h-first-class-local-reduction]]. Let $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_r$ be smooth gauge functions such that $A_{ab}=\{\chi_a,\phi_b\}$ is invertible on their common zero set near a point. Then the combined constraint matrix for $(\chi,\phi)$ is invertible there, so the combined surface is second class and carries the Dirac symplectic form. After shrinking the neighborhood, each nearby characteristic leaf intersects the gauge surface in exactly one point within that coordinate neighborhood. This is a local slice assertion only. When $r=0$ the characteristic leaves are points and the empty gauge condition is immediate; the proof below treats $r\ge1$.
thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesi:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with signature $(-+++)$. Work in a spacetime chart on a compact parameter interval $[a,b]$ with $a<b$; take $x,p,e$ smooth on a neighbourhood of that interval, $e>0$, $m\ge0$, and $c>0$. Select stationary triples on the future shell branch after taking the independent variations: when $m>0$, $p^\sharp$ is future timelike; when $m=0$, require $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ future null. Set $C_m=\tfrac12(g^{ab}p_ap_b+m^2c^2)$ and define the first-order functional

$$I_m[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left(p_ax'^a-eC_m(x,p)\right)d\lambda.$$

Take independent smooth variations of $p,e$ and fixed-endpoint variations of $x$. Stationarity on the chart segment is equivalent to

$$x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b,\quad p'_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c,\quad C_m=0.$$

On the massive future branch $m>0$, these equations are equivalent to stationary paths of the mathematical square-root functional $S[x]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-g(x\prime,x\prime)}\,d\lambda$ on future-timelike curves with fixed endpoints; the fibre-derivative covector is $p=mc\,x'^\flat/\sqrt{-g(x',x')}$, and proper-time gauge has $e=1/m$. In both cases the unparameterized path is a geodesic, and no existence or completeness claim is made.
thm-rpm-h-inertial-time-reduced-hamilton:
## Statement

In affine Minkowski space with $x^0=ct$, let $m\ge0$, $p_i$ be spatial momentum components and $p_i\ne0$ for $m=0$. On the future shell, $p_0=-E/c$, where

$$E(\mathbf p)=\sqrt{m^2c^4+c^2|\mathbf p|^2}.$$

On any compact interval $J=[t_1,t_2]$ of inertial time, the gauge $x^0=ct$ reduces the first-order shell action to

$$I_J=\int_{t_1}^{t_2}\left(p_i\dot q^i-E(\mathbf p)\right)dt,\qquad q^i=x^i.$$

The gauge pair $C_m=0$, $\psi=x^0-ct=0$ is second class because $\{C_m,\psi\}=-P^0\ne0$ on the future shell; its Dirac reduction gives the canonical spatial bracket. The reduced Hamilton equations are $\dot q^i=c^2p_i/E$, $\dot p_i=0$, agreeing with the unreduced characteristic trajectories. On this full flat future shell every characteristic line meets each inertial-time slice once; this global assertion does not extend by this proof to a curved temporal chart.

def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data:
## Definition

Assume countable choice ACω, as in [[def-countable-choice]], for the smooth cotangent-bundle carrier convention used by this page; no full Axiom of Choice is assumed.

Let $(M,g,T)$ be a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, with the geometric meaning fixed by [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].
